vaporPressure: ~0.002 mmHg at 20 °C (elemental Hg); ionic forms non-volatile
waterSolubility: Hg²⁺ salts highly soluble; HgCl₂ ~69 g/L at 20 °C
environmentalPersistence: Extremely high — mercury cycles globally; methylmercury persists and bioaccumulates in food chains

morphologicalEffects.heightSuppression: Strong — Hg is among the most potent root inhibitors of the heavy metals
morphologicalEffects.leafCurl: Mild to moderate — stomatal dysfunction causes some curling
morphologicalEffects.wilting: Strong — aquaporin inhibition by Hg²⁺ is one of its most distinctive mechanisms
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Strong — chloroplast ultrastructure damage; thylakoid membrane disruption
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Strong — root tip necrosis; dark spotting on leaves
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Both affected; wilting and chlorosis appear across canopy

physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Strongly reduced — Hg²⁺ blocks aquaporins in guard cells directly
physiologyEffects.transpiration: Strongly reduced — aquaporin blockage most distinctive Hg physiological effect
physiologyEffects.waterUptake: Severely impaired — aquaporin (PIP) inhibition is Hg's signature mechanism

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Strong — Hg has high affinity for thiol groups; disables antioxidant enzymes

microbiomeEffects.diversityReduction: Very strong — Hg is among the most toxic heavy metals to microbiome

temporalDynamics.recoveryTime: None — Hg binds irreversibly to thiol groups; permanent enzyme inactivation

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Green → yellow (chlorosis); rapid wilting; dark brown-black root deposits
visualSimulation.firstAffectedRegion: Roots first (wilting signal), then whole-canopy wilting
visualSimulation.damageSpread: Systemic via aquaporin blockage — rapid whole-plant wilting is distinctive
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Rapid wilting distinguishes Hg from other heavy metals; chlorosis follows
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Strong — Hg-cysteine and phytochelatin signature; distinctive from other heavy metals
visualSimulation.microbiomeParticles: Very sparse; near-zero diversity; high pathogen fraction
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: No recovery — permanent wilt and chlorosis

synergies.synergyNote: Mercury + cadmium: shared thiol-binding competition overwhelms GSH and phytochelatin detox systems; especially toxic combination
synergies.antagonismNote: Selenium can reduce Hg bioavailability via HgSe complex formation — not in the chemical list but worth noting for completeness

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Coal combustion (primary global source), artisanal gold mining, fluorescent lamps, industrial wastewater, thermometers
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: None — legacy use as fungicide (now banned); contaminant from atmospheric deposition
educationalContext.humanToxicity: Extremely high — methylmercury causes Minamata disease (neurological devastation); prenatal exposure causes severe developmental damage
educationalContext.climateLink: Mercury deposition increases near coal plants; climate-driven permafrost thaw releasing mercury stored for millennia
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Primarily outdoor (atmospheric deposition) and industrial; indoor from broken fluorescent lamps and old thermometers
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: The Minamata Bay disaster in Japan — one of the most dramatic environmental health catastrophes in history. Tuna and swordfish mercury contamination is relevant to students' food choices.
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Coal power pollution, artisanal gold mining, ocean food chain bioaccumulation, Minamata disease
